title: Ingress identity migration checklist and TF notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for migrating customer/on‑prem ingress to a new identity‑aware ingress proxy and associated network changes with near zero downtime. Focus areas: private DNS handling, NAT/egress continuity, firewall rule staged rollout, TF module changes, and validation tests.

Scope and constraints:
- Applies to private deployments (VPC + on‑prem hybrid) running our inference stack (gateway + envoy sidecars + inference pods).
- Must preserve existing client IP expectations for rate limiting and audit logs where possible.
- TLS certs are managed by customer KMS; rotation window is constrained.
- Target RTO < 5 minutes for a single‑region migration step.

High-level migration strategy (summary):
1) Introduce new ingress proxy in parallel (new TG / LB / instance group) behind a temporary hostname in the private DNS zone.
2) Configure proxy in passthrough mode to mirror existing path and headers while collecting telemetry.
3) Progressive traffic shifting via weighted DNS (private DNS TTL short) + ingress HA rules; do not change NAT/eProxy until canary passes.
4) Gradual promotion of new proxy to authoritative hostname, then retire old ingress after soak.

Prereqs / quick checklist before starting:
- Terraform plan applied to a staging VPC with identical networking rules.
- Private DNS zone editable and supports short TTLs (<= 30s for canary).
- Egress NAT capacity validated for burst + sticky IPs considered.
- Firewall rule audit and change window scheduled with security team.
- Observability: request latency, 5xx rate, TLS handshake errors, client IP preservation, conntrack usage.

Detailed steps:
A) Provisioning the new proxy (no traffic):
- TF: add new module instance ingress_proxy.new_proxy with feature_flags { identity_awareness = true, passthrough_mode = true }
- Allocate a non-production private hostname: ingress-migration-shadow.internal.example.com
- Create healthcheck endpoint /_probe/ingress-migration that returns 200 only when proxy has successfully synced config and identity upstream mapping.
- Wire ALB/NGINX/Envoy target group to new backend without modifying customer-facing DNS.

B) Identity validation and header preservation testing (shadow traffic):
- Enable transparent proxying: forward-client-ip header + x-forwarded-for preserved.
- Use internal load generator to send mirrored traffic to new proxy (no response to clients).
- Validate logged identity extraction (OIDC token or mTLS subject) matches expectations.
- Ensure rate limiting keys remain consistent (client IP or identity subject).

C) Canary traffic shift (controlled production traffic):
- Shorten private DNS TTL for target hostname to 10s.
- Update private DNS to include weighted A records pointing 5% to new proxy and 95% to old. Alternatively, use LB weights if DNS not flexible.
- Monitor metrics for 30–60 minutes. Have a rollback DNS map ready.

D) NAT and egress continuity notes:
- If NAT IP sticky behavior is required by downstream licensing, ensure new proxy egress path uses same SNAT pool or add header X-Original-Nat-Ip (not ideal).
- Terraform: do not replace existing nat_gateway resource; create nat_gateway.ingress_migration and add route rules incrementally.
- For on‑prem with limited SNAT IPs, apply connection draining (graceful) and conntrack drain before switching heavy traffic.

E) Firewall rule staged rollout (least blast radius):
- Use allow-lists keyed by resource tags (ingress:old, ingress:new) so we can flip network-policy rules by tag instead of editing individual rules.
- Steps: 1) add ingress:new allow rules in parallel 2) monitor for unexpected source IPs 3) after soak, remove ingress:old rules.
- Keep temporary audit rule that logs allowed connections for 72h to catch overlooked flows.

F) Private DNS handling specifics:
- Don't delete old A/AAAA records — canonical name change via CNAME is preferred where internal DNS supports it.
- If CNAME not supported for internal services, use DNS SRV for stage tagging or add secondary A with lower priority weight.
- TTL recommendations: pre-migration 300s, during canary 10–30s, post-migration 300s.
- If clients cache older DNS aggressively, plan for a 2–3 day tail and schedule final cutover accordingly.

Terraform module changes (notes to TF author):
- New module: modules/ingress-proxy-v2
  - variables: identity_mode (string: passthrough|enforce), nat_snat_pool_id (string), private_hostname (string), healthcheck_path (string)
  - outputs: lb_dns_name, tg_ids, applied_ruleset_id
- Avoid in-place replace of nat_gateway resource. Use new resource nat_gateway.migration_pool and a migration plan that updates route tables to include both gateways in a weighted/priority manner where cloud provider supports it.
- Add lifecycle.ignore_changes for aws_lb.target_group["old_proxy"].health_check to avoid noisy diffs during migration.
- TF sample var names (use these to coordinate ops runbooks):
  - var.ingress_proxy_identity_mode
  - var.ingress_proxy_private_host
  - var.ingress_proxy_snat_pool
  - var.ingress_migration_enabled (bool)

Validation tests and runbook checks:
- Smoke tests: simple 1k requests at 10rps; assert 99th percentile latency within baseline + 20%.
- Golden path: synthesize minimal auth token and ensure identity header downstream matches original pipeline.
- Negative test: send malformed JWT and verify proxy rejects with 401 and old proxy behavior is consistent.
- E2E: run a canary job that exercises full inference path and validates identical inference output for a small prompt set.

Rollback criteria and actions:
- Immediate rollback triggers: >2x 5xx rate, TLS handshake errors >0.5%, sustained latency p95 > 2x baseline for 30 minutes, or client IP loss for any critical tenant.
- Rapid rollback steps: revert private DNS weight to old proxy (increase old weight to 100%), disable new proxy identity enforcement, drain and deprovision new TG after 15 minute graceful window.

Operational notes / gotchas (lessons learned):
- Some on‑prem clients pin connections beyond DNS TTL; include a sidecar that accepts SIGHUP and closes long lived connections during cutover.
- Conntrack table exhaustion often appears during switch; keep spare NAT instances and monitor conntrack_count per instance.
- Firewall rule audits frequently miss internal platform tooling (monitoring agents) — include those IPs in allow-lists early.

Metrics and dashboards to create before migration:
- Ingress: requests/s, 4xx/s, 5xx/s, p50/p95/p99 latency, TLS handshake errors per minute, client_ip_missing_count
- Egress: SNAT usage per pool, conntrack count, retransmits
- Proxy: identity extraction success rate, auth failures, header drop rate

Post-cutover checklist (first 48h):
- Keep both proxy logs archived for at least 7 days and run weekly diff of identity maps for 2 weeks.
- Confirm no regression in cost (NAT egress + LB peak) compared to baseline.
- Schedule a retro with security, SRE, and product to capture gaps.

Open action items (todo):
- Diego: add TF module skeleton and open PR for internal review (ENG-2981).
- Marcus: create private DNS pre-req edit permission ticket with infra team.
- Aisha: run staging canary and paste results into this doc after 2025-11-10 run.

Notes to self (informal):
- If we need deterministic client IP for audits, plan to keep original proxy in path as a transparent pass-through for audit logs for 7 days after migration.
- Consider adding a short lived header X-Ingress-Proxy-V (value=v2) to help post-migration traffic labeling for easier queries.

Example quick commands (ops):
- TF plan: terraform plan -var-file=env/prod.tfvars -target=module.ingress_proxy.new_proxy
- Healthcheck curl: curl -vkS --resolve ingress-migration-shadow.internal.example.com:443:10.10.0.12 https://ingress-migration-shadow.internal.example.com/_probe/ingress-migration
- DNS update (bind9 example): nsupdate -k /etc/rndc.key <<EOF
server dns.internal
zone internal.example.com
update add ingress.internal.example.com 10 IN A 10.10.0.12
send
EOF

References and reading:
- Internal: Confluence page above (linked).
- Past incidents: see postmortem ENG-1772 (conntrack exhaustion during egress change).

End of draft.

-- a.p.
